title: Boatwright debuts strong as Gilas routs Syria in FIBA World Cup qualifiers
summary: New naturalized Filipino Bennie Boatwright and star center Kai Sotto live up to the hype as Gilas Pilipinas pummels Syria to kick off its fifth-window campaign in the 2027 FIBA World Cup Asian…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Syria had no answer to the towering might and pinpoint shooting of Gilas Pilipinas as the favored Filipino squad rolled to a dominant 97-58 win to begin its campaign in the 2027 FIBA World Cup Asian qualifiers fifth window in Seremban, Malaysia on Friday, November 27.

Long-awaited naturalized player Bennie Boatwright made sure to live up to the hype in his national team debut, tallying a big double-double of 16 points and 13 rebounds, while frontcourt partner Kai Sotto led the new twin-tower duo with 18 points and 10 boards in just 17 minutes.

“We only had a few practices with Bennie Boatwright, and yet, he’s fitting into us like a glove,” said Gilas head coach Tim Cone. “He didn’t go out and force anything, and stayed in what we do. From a coaching standpoint, you like it, because it wasn’t guys stepping out of what they do, it was really within what we’ve asked them to do, and that was really nice.”

“I just think that the more Bennie is with us, the more he’ll get comfortable, and know where his teammates are, and know where they like to get the ball. We’ll know more about him as we go along. We just see him elevating his game more and more when he’s with us.”

While Boatwright and Sotto set the tone in the first half on the way to a 43-32 lead, star forward Kevin Quiambao seized the spotlight in the latter two frames, as he led an offensive onslaught from deep to finish with a game-high-tying 18 points, all off a 6-of-8 shooting spree from three.

Thanks to a 29-13 third quarter pullaway that featured a 6-of-7 team clip from downtown, Gilas fully negated its slow start to lead by as many as 40, 95-55, and rise to a 5-4 record in Group E. Syria, meanwhile, stayed at the bottom of the six-nation group with a 2-7 card.
“These games this late in the qualifying, this late window five of six windows, they are so absolutely crucial at this point. We brought by far our best team, I think,” Cone said.

“Our size kind of took over the game at some point. We just controlled the boards. I think we won it like, 60-30, or something like that. When you could do that, you can run up the score, and we were able to run up the score.”After losing to undefeated Australia (9-0), earlier in the day, 84-67, Iran fell to a 5-4 slate ahead of its crucial clash on Sunday, November 29, against Gilas, which now enjoys a three-game winning streak after losing four straight.

A sweep of the Malaysia leg can put the Philippines on top of its Iranian rivals to boost its chances of World Cup qualification after a stretch of heartbreaking windows. Gilas ends its qualifying run at home in Cebu City in late February 2027.
Gilas Pilipinas 97 – Sotto 18, Quiambao 18, Boatwright 16, Gomez de Liaño 11, Perez 10, Phillips 10, Ramos 5, Edu 4, Millora-Brown 4, Newsome 1, Thompson 0, Rosario 0.
Syria 58 – Atli 12, Harrison 10, Albalbisi 9, Idelbi 6, Hermes 6, Maran 6, Abdullah, Y. 5, Michelsson 4, Nounou 0, Abdullah, K. 0, Majak 0.
